one_liner: A court reporter who takes down House floor debates, hearings and markups word-for-word at high speed and produces edited official transcripts.
fit_summary: This is a skilled stenography job that requires extensive experience reporting multi-voice hearings at very high speeds, and NCRA or state certification is strongly preferred. Nothing on file shows Daniel has machine-shorthand training or court-reporting experience. Daniel's knowledge of Congress and politics is a real plus, but it cannot substitute for the core stenographic skill.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring path: public), so no prior federal status is needed.
Requires extensive knowledge and experience in reporting, plus the ability to report multi-voice hearings at very high speeds.
An NCRA proficiency certification or a similar state certification is strongly preferred.
A Top Secret national security clearance is required, and this is a Test Designated Position subject to random drug testing.
This is a House (legislative branch) HS-12 position, so executive-branch time-in-grade rules do not apply.
keywords: Rules and procedures of the House
strategy: Be honest with yourself first: apply only if you actually have stenographic or voice-writing skills at professional speed. Otherwise, treat this as a signal of a possible long-term path (court-reporting school plus NCRA RPR), not a current target.
If you have reporting skills, list your certification, your certified speed in words per minute, and any realtime capability at the top of a two-page resume, with hours per week for each job.

Frame your IEM work around transcription-adjacent tasks you really did, such as documenting government meetings, drafting after-action reports or minutes, editing deliverables to a style guide, and handling sensitive client information.
Highlight your command of House procedure and the legislative process (for example markups, amendments, motions, and the Congressional Record), which the posting calls expert knowledge.
Prepare for the structured interview with STAR examples showing tact with varied personalities, working under pressure, and long or irregular hours.
The posting closes 2027-01-01, but House offices often review applications as they arrive, so apply early and note any prior clearance eligibility.
resume_bullets: Reported/transcribed [number] [type of proceedings] at [speed] wpm with [accuracy %], delivering edited transcripts within [turnaround time].
At IEM, documented [meetings/exercises] for [government client], producing [minutes/after-action reports] edited to [style guide] under [deadline].
Handled [sensitive/confidential] client materials in accordance with [policy/clearance level], maintaining [result you can verify].
interview_questions: What certification and realtime speed do you hold, and how do you handle multi-voice crosstalk in a hearing?
How would you reflect a motion to recommit or a unanimous consent request accurately in a transcript?
Describe a time you met a tight deadline after a long day while keeping accuracy high.
How do you protect classified or confidential material in your work?
watch_outs: The core requirement is high-speed verbatim reporting, a specialized skill Daniel is not known to have.
A Top Secret clearance and random drug testing are required.
The role requires long hours, nights, and weekends, with no telework, plus a commute from Manassas to the Capitol.
NCRA or state certification is strongly preferred, and acquiring one takes years of training.
